Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Notice on Issuing the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Sentencing Circumstances such as Voluntary Surrender and Meritorious Service in Handling Duty Crime Cases"

Fa Fa [2009] No. 13

The High People's Courts and People's Procuratorates of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court and the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Sentencing Circumstances such as Voluntary Surrender and Meritorious Service in Handling Duty Crime Cases of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate are hereby issued to you. Please implement them earnestly.

March 12, 2009

Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Sentencing Circumstances such as Voluntary Surrender and Meritorious Service in Handling Duty Crime Cases

To lawfully punish duty crimes such as embezzlement, bribery, and malfeasance, in accordance with the Criminal Law and relevant judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual work of handling cases, the following opinions are put forward regarding the determination and handling of sentencing circumstances such as voluntary surrender and meritorious service in handling duty crime cases:

I. Determination and Handling of Voluntary Surrender

According to Article 67, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, the establishment of voluntary surrender requires the simultaneous satisfaction of two elements: voluntarily surrendering oneself and truthfully confessing one's own crimes. When the criminal facts or the criminal have not been known to the case-handling authority, or although known, the criminal has not yet been subject to investigative interviews or interrogations, or has not been announced as subject to investigative measures or compulsory measures, surrendering to the case-handling authority constitutes voluntarily surrendering oneself. If the criminal truthfully confesses their main criminal facts during this period, it shall be deemed as voluntary surrender.

If a criminal surrenders to units other than the case-handling authority, such as the unit to which they belong, or to other organizations or responsible persons, it shall be regarded as voluntarily surrendering oneself.

If the criminal does not voluntarily surrender, but during the period of investigative interviews, interrogations, investigative measures, or compulsory measures by the case-handling authority, they truthfully confess the facts targeted by the leads already known to the case-handling authority, this cannot be deemed as voluntary surrender.

If the criminal does not voluntarily surrender but falls under any of the following circumstances, it shall be treated as voluntary surrender: (1) The criminal truthfully confesses crimes not known to the case-handling authority that are of a different type from the crimes already known to the case-handling authority; (2) The criminal facts targeted by the leads known to the case-handling authority are not established, and the criminal confesses crimes of the same type beyond this scope.

In cases of unit crime, if the unit voluntarily surrenders through a collective decision or a decision by the person in charge of the unit and truthfully confesses the unit's criminal facts, or if the directly responsible supervisor of the unit voluntarily surrenders and truthfully confesses the unit's criminal facts, it shall be deemed as voluntary surrender by the unit. In the case of voluntary surrender by the unit, if the directly responsible supervisor and directly responsible personnel do not voluntarily surrender but truthfully confess the criminal facts known to them, this may be regarded as voluntary surrender; if they refuse to confess the criminal facts known to them or evade legal accountability, it shall not be deemed as voluntary surrender. If the unit does not make voluntary surrender, but the directly responsible personnel voluntarily surrenders and truthfully confesses the criminal facts known to them, the directly responsible personnel shall be deemed as having made voluntary surrender.

For criminals with the circumstance of voluntary surrender, the case-handling authority shall explain this and transfer relevant evidence materials when transferring the case.

For criminals with the circumstance of voluntary surrender, a decision shall be made in accordance with the law on whether to impose a lighter or mitigated punishment or to exempt punishment, and the extent of such lighter or mitigated punishment, based on the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of harm to society of the crime, combined with specific circumstances such as the motive, stage, and objective environment of the voluntary surrender, the completeness and stability of the confession, and the expression of repentance.

II. Determination and Handling of Meritorious Service

Meritorious service must be an act personally performed by the criminal. If, in order to obtain a lighter punishment for the criminal, the criminal's relatives or friends directly expose others' criminal acts to the relevant authorities, provide important leads for solving other cases, or assist the judicial authorities in arresting other criminal suspects, this shall not be deemed as meritorious service by the criminal.

The materials on others' crimes relied upon for meritorious service shall specify the specific criminal facts; the leads or assistive acts relied upon for meritorious service shall have a practical effect on solving the case or arresting the criminal suspect. If the criminal, when exposing others' criminal acts, does not specify the specific criminal facts; if the exposed criminal facts are not related to the verified criminal facts; or if the provided leads or assistive acts have no practical effect on solving other cases or arresting other criminal suspects, it cannot be deemed as meritorious service.

If a criminal exposes others' criminal acts or provides important leads for solving other cases, this must be verified to be true before it can be deemed as meritorious service. When reviewing whether meritorious service is established, not only the explanatory materials of the case-handling authority shall be examined, but also the relevant facts and evidence, as well as legal documents related to the characterization and punishment of the case, such as the decision to place a case on file, the arrest decision, the investigation termination report, the prosecution opinion, the indictment, or the judgment.

If the leads or material sources relied upon for meritorious service fall under any of the following circumstances, it cannot be deemed as meritorious service: (1) Obtained by the criminal through illegal means or channels; (2) Obtained by the criminal due to their former duties of investigating and prohibiting crimes; (3) Provided to the criminal by others in violation of regulatory provisions; (4) Provided by state functionaries with the duty to investigate and prohibit criminal activities or other state functionaries taking advantage of their positions.

If the criminal reported or exposed others' crimes, provided important leads for solving other cases, prevented others' criminal activities, or assisted the judicial authorities in arresting other criminal suspects, and such criminal suspect, defendant, or criminal is legally subject to a punishment of life imprisonment or above, it shall be deemed as a major meritorious service. Among these, "legally subject to a punishment of life imprisonment or above" means that based on the facts and circumstances of the criminal act, a punishment of life imprisonment or above may be imposed. If the case has already been adjudicated, the actual punishment imposed shall prevail. However, if according to the facts and circumstances of the criminal act, a punishment of life imprisonment or above should have been imposed, but due to the sentenced person's statutory circumstances, a lighter or mitigated punishment was lawfully imposed resulting in a fixed-term imprisonment, this shall be deemed as major meritorious service.

For criminals with the circumstance of meritorious service, a decision shall be made in accordance with the law on whether to impose a lighter or mitigated punishment or to exempt punishment, and the extent of such lighter or mitigated punishment, based on the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of harm to society of the crime, combined with specific circumstances such as the degree of effectiveness of the meritorious act, the severity of the crimes solved, the statutory punishment likely to be imposed on the arrested criminal suspect, and the timing of the meritorious act.

III. Determination and Handling of Truthfully Confessing Criminal Facts

If a criminal does not legally establish voluntary surrender but truthfully confesses criminal facts under any of the following circumstances, a lighter punishment may be considered on a discretionary basis: (1) The case-handling authority has grasped part of the criminal facts, and the criminal confesses other criminal facts of the same type; (2) The evidence grasped by the case-handling authority is insufficient, and the criminal's truthful confession helps in collecting evidence for finalizing the case.

If a criminal truthfully confesses criminal facts under any of the following circumstances, a lighter punishment shall generally be imposed: (1) The case-handling authority has only grasped a small part of the criminal facts, and the criminal confesses most of the criminal facts of the same type not yet grasped; (2) The truthful confession plays an important role in collecting evidence for finalizing the case.

IV. Handling of Circumstances such as Recovery of Illicit Gains and Proceeds

In cases of embezzlement, if all or most of the illicit gains and proceeds have been recovered, a lighter punishment shall generally be considered.

In cases of bribery, if all or most of the illicit gains and proceeds have been recovered, a lighter punishment may be considered on a discretionary basis depending on the specific circumstances.

If the criminal or their relatives voluntarily return the illicit gains or actively cooperate during the case-handling authority's recovery of illicit gains and proceeds, this shall be distinguished in sentencing from cases where the case-handling authority recovers illicit gains and proceeds ex officio during the investigation process.

After a duty crime case is filed, the economic losses recovered by the criminal or their relatives on their own, the economic losses recovered by the judicial authorities or the unit to which the criminal belongs and its superior departments, or the economic losses reduced due to objective reasons, shall not be deducted but may be considered as a circumstance for discretionary lighter punishment.
